topic: Exact selective holdout-power design for two-stratum, two-stage enrichment at a prespecified sharp zero-effect null. Use complete randomization within stratum and stage, an independent exchangeable simple-random stage-1 holdout with rho in a fixed compact interval, and an uncentered standardized treated-minus-control recruitment selector with fixed threshold. On a uniform local-pair-spacing finite-population class with fixed positive-margin selection cells and finite jointly realizable Gaussian primitives, optimize worst-cell conditional local power over compact positive alternatives and nonnegative unit-norm cell-specific stage weights. Prove the selected-quantile convexity reduction, Delta=A-kappa*b1 weight-side theorem, all-nonnegative-Delta unique largest-holdout result, certified negative-Delta interior regime, and complete mixed-sign analytic branch geometry. State equality strata symbolically; give tolerance-certified value and optimizer-set boxes generally and unique designs only with an explicit separation certificate. Consumer: continuous-outcome FOURIER-style future enrichment designs using exact selective randomization inference. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Ehrhard convexity makes the selected-score quantiles convex and reduces every above-size optimizing comparison over an arbitrary compact positive alternative set to its least coordinate. In the exchangeable square-root path, a Mills-ratio factorization proves that Delta determines which side of the proportional stage weight contains every optimum; a realizability bound then makes the largest allowed holdout uniquely optimal when all retained cells have nonnegative Delta. A 100-bit Arb certificate gives a legal negative-Delta mixture whose interior design has power above 0.86428621266 while both endpoint continua stay below 0.86304573855. Symbolic equality predicates and tolerance boxes avoid the refuted exact-real zero oracle. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Establish the uniform split-conditional Gaussian and zero-null reference transfer with common finite-population remainder, including random complement counts, studentization, rank stability, and conditional quantile transfer. EARLY KILL TEST: Independently verify the Ehrhard-to-quantile single-crossing reduction, then prove the reference approximation on one bounded nonproportional baseline family; pivot if additional population assumptions are necessary. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/exp_selective_holdout_power_frontier.md.

open_problems.why_unsolved: The available components inhabit incompatible regimes. Finite-population CLTs and Berry–Esseen bounds control unconditional permutation statistics, whereas selective Gaussian-transfer results assume independent sampling and smooth external randomization. Here the selector, test statistic, studentizer, and random holdout-complement counts are dependent without-replacement statistics, and stage-2 recruitment is determined by the selected stage-1 cell. Converting one joint approximation into conditional cdf and quantile control requires a common remainder, uniform studentizer consistency, positive lower bounds for selection-cell probabilities, anti-concentration at moving thresholds, and rank/count stability. Prior CausalSmith work independently identified weighted Gaussian transport and uniform self-normalization as unresolved rather than routine consequences of a scalar CLT.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform theorem bounding the conditional cdf, studentized pivot, and selected-quantile errors between the finite-population statistic/reference pair and a jointly realizable Gaussian analogue over the population class, compact holdout interval, nonnegative unit weights, positive-margin cells, and compact local alternatives, using one explicit or vanishing common remainder.

writing_exemplar.why: Its enrichment example exposes the gap between exact selective validity and model-based Gaussian power analysis.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Conditioning validates an adaptively selected experiment -> holdouts retain assignment information for inference -> power design needs tractable selected laws -> a uniform finite-population-to-Gaussian transfer is required.

method_exemplars.why_closest: The selector, stage contrasts, holdout counts, and studentizers can first be embedded in one finite-population contrast vector before conditioning.

method_exemplars.technique: Transfer a pre-selection Gaussian approximation through randomized selection by controlling the selection likelihood and conditional law.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the conditional-transfer proof architecture; the new step is replacing iid smooth randomization by simple-random holdout and complete-randomization combinatorics.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent complete-randomization estimators as linear permutation statistics and combine Stein-method Berry–Esseen bounds with variance-estimator concentration.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its quantitative unconditional remainder is the natural input to conditional cdf and quantile transfer once selection probabilities and anti-concentration are controlled.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Selective randomization inference proves validity for arbitrary admissible selectors and tests but leaves holdout allocation and powerful selection-dependent statistics open; existing enrichment optimization is numerical and model-based. The scoped literature contains no analytic maximin result coupling holdout information loss, selected critical values, and cell-specific stage weights. The unverified presolve route still requires two nonstandard steps: deriving a single-crossing least-coordinate reduction from Gaussian quantile convexity, and proving that the sign pattern of Delta=A-kappa*b1 exhausts the proportional-side, endpoint, interior, and mixed-sign branches. Prior CausalSmith work also shows that a floating-point optimizer is insufficient when equality strata or continua are possible: the entire optimizer set must be certified after the finite-population transfer error is included.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A complete analytic characterization of the maximin value and argmax correspondence, including the selected-quantile convexity reduction, Delta-indexed weight-side restriction, uniquely optimal largest holdout under all nonnegative Delta, a certified negative-Delta interior regime, complete mixed-sign branch geometry, symbolic equality strata, and tolerance-certified value and optimizer-set boxes.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates holdouts as information-preserving devices for selective randomization inference and explicitly poses their allocation as a power-design problem.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Adaptive enrichment invalidates naive randomization inference -> conditioning restores exact selective validity -> holdouts preserve unused randomization information -> their fraction and analysis weights should be optimized for conditional power.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt Ehrhard–Borell Gaussian-measure convexity and its equality-case analysis to conditional selected-score sublevel sets and their quantile map.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed least-coordinate reduction requires convexity and equality information for Gaussian selection probabilities, not merely differentiability of a power formula.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent two-stage selection and testing policies through trajectories and optimize power/error constraints using a sparse finite-dimensional program.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest two-stratum, two-stage power-design benchmark and can provide numerical cross-checks for the desired analytic argmax correspondence.

method_exemplars.technique: Condition the randomization distribution on the realized adaptive design and preserve inference-only assignment information through holdout units.
method_exemplars.why_closest: This is the exact validity mechanism whose conditional local power the new design characterization must optimize.

open_problems.why_unsolved: A weak null does not impute missing potential outcomes, and conditioning on the selected enrichment cell changes both the sampling law and the imputed sharp-null reference law. Nonselective studentization and Gaussian prepivoting use unconditional covariance or stochastic-dominance comparisons; division by a selection probability can destroy those comparisons. The first unresolved step is therefore a conditional dominance theorem comparing the heterogeneous-effect sampling law with the sharp-null randomization law after both are restricted to the same adaptive recruitment event.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A studentized or Gaussian-prepivoted selective randomization procedure that is finite-sample exact at the sharp null and uniformly conditionally conservative for a weak cell-specific finite-population average-effect null, with a conditional limit law and an invertible confidence set.

writing_exemplar.why: It states the sharp-null and homogeneous-effect limitations in the exact adaptive-enrichment setting.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Selective randomization validates inference for a data-chosen subgroup -> the sharp null excludes scientifically relevant heterogeneous effects -> weak-null validity must be reconciled with adaptive-selection conditioning.

method_exemplars.technique: Push a sample-based Gaussian measure through the test statistic, enumerate the sharp-null randomization distribution, and prove weak-null stochastic dominance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired resolution needs the same sharp-exact and weak-asymptotic bridge, with every comparison additionally conditional on the selected cell.

method_exemplars.technique: Impute under a compatible sharp null, studentize finite-population contrasts, and compare sampling and permutation limits.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its stratified finite-population studentization is directly relevant, but must be rebuilt for adaptive recruitment counts and selective conditioning.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Conditioning on an exactly selected continuous cutoff may reveal essentially all stage-1 assignment information, so the selective test loses its carving advantage. Gao's self-contained rule treats subgroup selection in a fixed trial, while model-based two-stage enrichment methods exploit nested covariance without characterizing the assignments remaining feasible after the cutoff determines recruitment. The first new proof step is a combinatorial support characterization for assignments compatible with each cutoff, followed by a uniform lower bound on residual assignment entropy as the cutoff grid grows.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A characterization of cutoff selectors and holdout fractions for which every retained selection cell leaves a positive asymptotic fraction of stage-1 assignments feasible, together with an exact selective p-value and a nondegenerate conditional local-power limit.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames continuous-cutoff selection as a double-use problem and makes retention of selected-subgroup information the central payoff.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Biomarker cutoffs target treatment heterogeneity -> selecting and testing on the same assignments invalidates naive inference -> self-contained selection retains information in a fixed trial -> two-stage recruitment needs an analogous support-preserving rule.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct a self-contained cutoff rule whose conditioning event permits a tractable randomization test using all units in the selected subgroup.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It solves the fixed-trial version of the information-retention problem; the destination adds adaptive stage-2 recruitment and holdout optimization.

method_exemplars.technique: Exploit nesting of threshold-defined subgroups to represent their statistics as a sequential Gaussian process and compute rejection probabilities.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The nested-score covariance representation can supply the local-power process after exact selective conditioning and support preservation are established.

open_problems.open_problem: What positive-margin or shrinking-margin modulus guarantees rank stability of the uncentered recruitment selector and uniform transfer of selected local power, and where does such stability fail?

source_refs.excerpt: state the accompanying external-score envelope needed to control generated rank switches uniformly
the selected law, sharp modulus, and computable uniformly valid interval remain open

open_problems.why_unsolved: The banked selection-boundary work shows that pointwise score approximation and ordinary moment regularity do not control data-dependent rank switches; a uniform coercivity or score-envelope condition is needed. For randomized enrichment, the first proof step changes from linearizing an estimated external-control ranking to coupling a finite-population recruitment score with its Gaussian reference. A fixed margin may stabilize the cell, but its rate must jointly dominate Gaussian approximation, studentization, and random-complement errors. No inspected proposal establishes that combined implication or a sharp failure boundary.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A margin-indexed bound on selector-cell mismatch probability and conditional-law distance, together with either a sharp shrinking-margin rate frontier or a finite-population counterexample showing failure below that frontier.

writing_exemplar.why: Its adaptive-enrichment formulation makes the selected recruitment cell and the assignments compatible with it first-class inferential objects.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Recruitment depends on a randomized stage-1 score -> inference conditions on the resulting cell -> nearby score boundaries can change that cell under small perturbations -> uniform validity requires an explicit margin-to-stability modulus.

method_exemplars.technique: Control the selection likelihood while transferring asymptotic normality through randomized selection.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired modulus similarly must convert pre-selection approximation into selected-law approximation, but for discontinuous cells and without-replacement assignment.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt post-selection nonuniformity arguments to construct local sequences on which selector stability or conditional-law estimation fails.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A sharp shrinking-margin frontier requires both a stable regime and a matching boundary counterexample.

literature_map:
Freidling, Zhao, and Gao (2026, JRSSB; arXiv:2405.07026) establish exact selective randomization inference for adaptive experiments and use two-stratum enrichment as a running example.
They explicitly leave holdout size, stage placement, adaptive-design power, and most-powerful selection-dependent statistics open.
Their discussion also identifies weak-null inference and continuous-biomarker recruitment as unresolved extensions.
Rosenblum, Fang, and Liu (2020, JRSSB) optimize two-stage enrichment rules through sparse linear programming, yielding a numerical model-based benchmark rather than analytic conditional-randomization geometry.
Ondra et al. (2019, Statistical Methods in Medical Research) provide decision-theoretic enrichment optimization, reinforcing the distinction between utility optimization and exact selected-power design.
Zhang and Gao (2025, arXiv:2504.21572) adaptively split observations between CATE estimation and testing, but do not characterize exchangeable holdout fractions through conditional local-power geometry.
Li and Ding (2017, JASA; arXiv:1610.04821) supply general vector finite-population CLTs for randomization-based causal statistics.
Shi and Ding (2025 revision, arXiv:2209.12345) add quantitative Berry–Esseen bounds for linear and quadratic complete-randomization statistics and variance estimation.
Tian and Taylor (2018, Annals of Statistics; arXiv:1507.06739) transfer Gaussian limits through randomized selection under iid sampling, leaving the without-replacement conditional bridge unresolved.
Chen and Andrews (2023, arXiv:2309.12162) study optimal conditional inference in adaptive experiments under parametric superpopulation structure rather than fixed finite-population randomization.
Wu and Ding (2021, JASA; arXiv:1809.07419) obtain sharp-null exactness and weak-null asymptotic validity through studentized randomization tests in nonselective designs.
Cohen and Fogarty (2022, JRSSB; arXiv:2002.06654) use Gaussian prepivoting when studentization alone cannot provide weak-null dominance.
Caughey, Dafoe, Li, and Miratrix (2023, JRSSB; arXiv:2101.09195) extend exact randomization inference to bounded nulls and individual-effect quantiles without adaptive selection.
Gao (2025, arXiv:2504.19380) constructs self-contained continuous-biomarker subgroup selectors, while Stallard (2023, Biometrics) treats nested cutoff enrichment through Gaussian-process approximations.
Shenfeld and van Handel (2018, Advances in Mathematics; arXiv:1709.00061) settle Ehrhard–Borell equality cases, providing the natural convexity machinery for—but no existing application to—selected-score quantile and holdout-power geometry.
